candidates.change_summary: Remove the assignment 'owner = _owner;' so owner is never updated.
Change assignment to set owner to a different address, e.g., msg.sender instead of _owner.
Change the return value but also fail to update owner by returning early or assigning zero address.
Insert a statement that overrides the assignment, for example setting owner to a constant address after the line.
Remove the onlyAdmin modifier from setOwner so anyone can change owner.
Change the require condition to always pass, e.g. require(true), so that onlyAdmin no longer restricts access.
Change the require condition to use owner instead of admin, allowing owner (and not necessarily admin) to call setOwner.
Replace `return true;` with `return false;` so that the return value differs when the call succeeds.
Remove the `onlyAdmin` modifier from the function signature so that the call succeeds for any sender, but still returns `true`, changing the behavior for non-admin callers.
Replace the require condition with one that always passes (`require(true)`) so that unauthorized callers execute the function and return `true`, changing the behavior for non-admin callers.
Replace `owner = _owner;` with `owner = address(0);` so the new owner is not set to the argument.

Replace `owner = _owner;` with `owner = payable(_owner);` (no effect when owner is address, but owner is declared `address`, so this may not compile; safer: replace with a constant different from `_owner`, e.g., `address(0)` already covered; this mutant is invalid per instruction to compile). Actually, changing to `owner = address(uint160(_owner) + 1);` alters the stored owner.
Replace `return true;` with `return false;` so the return value differs.
Replace `require(msg.sender == admin, ...);` with `require(true, ...);` to remove the admin check.
Replace `require(msg.sender == admin, ...);` with `require(false, ...);` so the modifier always reverts.
Delete the require statement, leaving the modifier body empty (only `_;` remains).
